Roots to Grow Wings to Fly
Alfriston is a day and boarding school for girls catering for pupils with a wide range of special educational needs and disabilities, between the ages of 11 and 18.
Roots to Grow Wings to Fly
Alfriston is a day and boarding school for girls catering for pupils with a wide range of special educational needs and disabilities, between the ages of 11 and 18.
Welcome to Alfriston
Message from the Head
It is my privilege to welcome you to Alfriston School. Since joining as Headteacher in September 2024, I have been inspired every day by the resilience, curiosity, and ambition of our students and the unwavering commitment of our staff and families.
Alfriston is a specialist secondary school for girls aged 11–18, all of whom have an Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP). Our students’ primary need is moderate learning difficulties, and many also have additional communication and interaction needs. We are proud to provide a safe, inclusive environment where every student is valued, supported, and empowered to thrive.
Our vision is clear:“To empower students to navigate the world with a strong sense of purpose, identity and curiosity.”
This vision shapes every aspect of our work—from our curriculum design to our integrated therapeutic approaches, which include speech and language therapy, occupational therapy, and social-emotional support.
At Alfriston, education is about more than qualifications. It is about belonging, respect, and representation. It is about helping each young person discover their strengths, overcome challenges, and prepare for adulthood with optimism and resilience. Our six core values—Ambition, Belonging, Respect, Representation, Integrity, and Curiosity—guide our culture and decisions every day.
We are currently in an exciting phase of transformation, strengthening our curriculum, embedding inclusive practices, and deepening partnerships with families and the wider community. Together, we are building a school where every student feels safe, seen, and supported to achieve their personal best.
Thank you for visiting our website and for sharing in our journey. We look forward to working with you to create a future full of opportunity, growth, and meaningful achievement for every student at Alfriston.
Claire Smart

Sports Partnership
South Bucks Sports Partnership
At Alfriston School, we host the Inclusive South Bucks School Sports Partnership, where our motto is ‘A Sporting Chance for Every Child’ – and our vision really is as simple as that.
We work with a number of primary, secondary and special needs schools to ensure EVERY child and young person has a positive experience of both physical activity and school sport, as well as access to a wide range of activities. We strongly believe that everyone has the right to access high quality PE, school sport and physical activity.
Inclusion Lead School
We are proud to be one of just 50 lead schools from across England that have been established and selected for our recognised expertise in engaging young disabled people in PE and Sport.
As Inclusion Champions, we lead the way in making PE and school sport open, fun, and meaningful. We work with schools to empower teachers, allowing them to feel confident and supported in making their PE lessons more inclusive, creating exciting and fair opportunities for friendly competition, and even providing inclusive leadership opportunities. Our goal is to raise pupil’s aspirations, build confidence, and help every child feel like they belong in the world of sport.
South Bucks School Games Organiser
It is a privilege for us to serve as a host, and be part of the network of South Bucks School Games Organisers. We are one of eight hosts from across Buckinghamshire and Milton Keynes, working with schools from across South Bucks, National Governing Bodies and the County Sports Partnership (LEAP) to provide lots of ways for young people across Bucks and Milton Keynes to take part in and compete with others across the county.
The School Games mission and vision is to:
We help open doors to sport and physical activity for every young person. Through our work with schools across South Bucks, we create fun, inclusive events and competitions where children of all abilities can join in, feel part of a team, and enjoy being active. Our role is to support and encourage schools, making it easier for everyone to offer exciting and meaningful sporting opportunities.
What does it mean to schools and students to be a part of Alfriston’s School Sports Partnership? Why not take it from them…
The Sports Partnership Team should be recognised for their exemplary dedication and tireless efforts in supporting all partnership schools. They consistently go above and beyond, providing invaluable advice and high-quality continuing professional development (CPD) for staff, which significantly enhances our pedagogical approaches to sports. Their initiatives create numerous exciting opportunities for all pupils, ensuring that every child is included and able to participate, regardless of their ability level… Their ability to motivate and engage pupils is commendable; they inspire them [the students] to become active participants in sports, instilling a sense of enthusiasm and teamwork. Overall, their contributions have been transformative for our schools, fostering a more inclusive and dynamic sports culture that benefits all students. We are incredibly grateful for their leadership and commitment to excellence.
On behalf of Sarah and the Dorney School community, I wanted to thank you [Alfriston School Sports Partnership Team] for all the effort you put into organising events and competitions for as many children as possible to participate. Your effort and hard work do not go unnoticed, and we wanted you to know that we are truly grateful.
I have spoken to a few of our children who took part in the swimming gala, the squash event and on Girls' Football Day, their enthusiasm and positivity were fantastic! I wish I could bottle these [feelings] to sell as this could be a wonderful sport fundraiser.
The support from the Sports Partnership has been invaluable. Their passion, knowledge and commitment are incredible. This makes working with them inspirational and fun! They have supported us on every step of our journey from implementing sensory circuits in PE, organising Sports days to developing active lunchtime clubs and many more. We could not have done it without the help from the Sports Partnership!
Everyone was very supportive, encouraging and inclusive, we all felt right at home.
Sponsorship Opportunities
We are always looking to increase the opportunities available to children and young people across South Bucks and beyond.
We are looking for companies that would be willing to sponsor both individual events, and / or the Sport Partnership as a whole. Your donations and sponsorship can help to shape the physical activity journey of a young person for life.

Careers Guidance
Whilst at Alfriston School, students learn the skills and attitudes required to enable them to become as independent as they can be and to prepare for adulthood. We aim for students to have an enriched and stimulating curriculum to give them every opportunity to reach their full potential. Alfriston School supports careers development through high quality and personalised work experience opportunities. We enjoy high quality relationships with a number of external organisations and local businesses to provide opportunities for students to work in ‘real’ settings. We are always looking for additional opportunities to inspire and educate our students about the world of work. If you think you could help please contact our Careers Leader.
Careers Leader
The Careers Leader for our school is Shelley Irvine and she can be contacted via the school office Tel: 01494 673740 or by email: shelley.irvine@alfristonschool.com
Careers Programme
At each stage of the learning journey, students are supported and encouraged to consider their future beyond school. Our Careers Programme lists some of the elements of careers information, advice and guidance that a student will encounter during their time with us.
Provider Access Statement
Alfriston School is committed to providing high quality careers guidance and advice. Our Provider Access Statement (below) gives details of how training providers can visit the school to offer eligible pupils information and advice about career pathways.
The Gatsby Benchmarks – what are they?
The Gatsby Benchmarks provide a world-class framework for career guidance, outlining the experiences and information each and every young person should have access to so that they can make an informed decision about their future. As schools and colleges begin to work towards the Gatsby Benchmarks, the Gatsby Foundation and The Careers & Enterprise Company have been asked how the Benchmarks should be used for schools and students with special educational needs and disabilities. Young people attending special schools have a very wide range of special educational needs and disabilities, from behavioural and learning difficulties to physical and sensory disability. We recognise that the Benchmarks set a high bar, but we believe that aspirations should be high for special schools, as they should be for mainstream schools.
For more information on the Gatsby benchmarks please click on the following link: www.goodcareerguidance.org.uk

Trips
At Alfriston, pupils are offered many opportunities to take part in a variety of educational trips and visits which take place both locally and further afield. All trips and visits support the curriculum and offer pupils opportunities to develop their self-esteem, social, moral, cultural, and physical abilities.
Trips and off-site visits are a normal part of the curriculum at Alfriston, and students regularly go on trips within the Local Learning Area, which for Alfriston is within the county of Buckinghamshire.
These trips take place during normal school hours and follow the school operating procedure. Parent’s will be asked to complete a “Consent to Local Off-Site Visits and Medical Treatment Form” for participation in these activities when their child is admitted to the school.
Trips outside of the Local Learning Area, or outside of school hours, require parental consent. Consent will also be requested for activities that need a higher level of risk management, such as visits that are adventurous, residential, and overseas.
We understand that visits are often challenging for the pupils. Every visit is planned with meticulous attention to the safety and comfort of each individual pupil. Parents are informed in advance of the details of the trip and the itinerary, prior to be asking for consent.
Only staff who have been assessed as suitably qualified and experienced are approved to supervise groups in a new environment. All trips are recorded on the school’s trip management system, Evolve.
Visits are monitored by the School’s Educational Visits Co-ordinator, the Head and the Governors. In addition, residential and adventurous activities are vetted and monitored by Buckinghamshire Council Offsite Visits Advisors.

SEN Provision
What kinds of special educational needs are provided for at Alfriston School?
Alfriston School is a special school academy for girls aged 11 – 19. The school has provision for 20 girls to board for 3 nights per week. The pupils’ primary needs are moderate learning difficulties and speech, language and communication needs. Pupils may also have other associated needs in areas such as social and emotional, sensory and physical difficulties.
What are the school’s policies for identification and assessment of pupils attending Alfriston School?
All pupils will have an Education Health Care Plan.
What are the arrangements for consulting parents and involving them in their child’s education?
At Alfriston we encourage parents to be included in the process of the education their children. This includes:
Initial visits to the school
Induction meetings
Parents’ Evenings
EHCP Annual Review meeting and report
School events and celebrations
Parental representation on the Governing Body
The opportunity to be a ‘Parent Rep’
Parent Workshops
Parent support group
What are the arrangements for consulting young people and involving them in their education?
We listen to our pupils and involve them in decisions about their education through:
Involvement in the Annual Review meetings
Regular Pastoral Support meetings
What are the arrangements for assessing and reviewing pupil progress?
Pupils’ progress is continually monitored by their subject teachers and Pastoral Tutors. Academic and personal progress is reviewed formally each academic year. All pupils have an individual education plan which is reviewed termly, and includes targets for other aspects of learning, such as independence and personal and social development.
How do we support our pupils in moving between phases of education and in preparing for adulthood?
We recognise that “moving on” can be difficult for our pupils and take steps to ensure that this is as smooth as possible.
When moving classes within school:
When leaving our school at the end of Year 11 or after Post 16:
Parents are informed in advance
What is our approach to teaching?
Our aim is to provide a safe and happy environment, where our pupils can grow in confidence and acquire the education and skills to achieve their full potential.
What adaptations are made to the curriculum?
As a special school, our entire curriculum is tailored to the special needs of our pupils.
What is the expertise and training of staff and how will specialist expertise be secured?
All our staff are experienced in teaching and supporting pupils with moderate learning difficulties, and have a wide range of expertise in subject specialisms and in areas of special need.
Whole staff training is regularly provided to ensure a high level of expertise in a wide range of specialist areas such as speech, language and communication, ASD, social and emotional difficulties and other associated needs.
The school has a performance management process which includes identifying training needs for all staff to improve the teaching and learning of pupils.
Specialist expertise is secured through the appointment of the following in-house professionals:
And through direct input from other external professionals as required such as:
Speech and Language Therapist
Occupational Therapist
Student Counsellor
Multi disciplinary therapists
Educational Psychologists
Social Workers
CAMHS professionals
Physiotherapists
Specialist Advisors
Future Focus (Connexions)
What support does the school provide for improving social and emotional development?
The school has a strong Pastoral system with each pupil assigned to a Pastoral group with a dedicated Pastoral Tutor who closely monitors each child’s personal development.
Pupils with particular social or emotional difficulties are referred to our Therapies Team, who assess their needs and provide an individual programme of support.
Pupils may also be referred on to other professionals as needed.
A high level of care and attention is paid to every child’s welfare and any issues are quickly identified and addressed. Opportunities to develop personal and social skills are built into the curriculum, as well as time given to explore feelings and experiences in a safe and supportive environment.
Who can I contact for further information about our special education needs?
If you are an existing parent or carer the first point of contact is your daughter’s Pastoral Tutor.
If you are a prospective parent or carer, then please contact the school office.

New Parents
Transitioning from primary school to secondary school is a big and exciting step! However, we understand that it can be a daunting one too. We’ve compiled a list of frequently asked questions to help ease your mind prior to your child’s transition to Alfriston.
FAQ’s
Admissions and Transition
All admissions to Alfriston school come to us from the Local Authority, Buckinghamshire County Council.
Pupils are offered a transition programme prior to School Transition Day which typically comprises of two visits to Alfriston School with their parents / carers. In July we take part in the county-wide School Transition Day. This day allows pupils transitioning from Year 6 to Year 7 to experience a range of activities with their new peers and to meet members of staff prior to starting in September.
Students are also offered an in-depth induction upon their entry in the Autumn Term.
For more information on admissions and transitions, please see our Admissions page.

School Lunches
Lunch time meals are provided by Thomas Franks – our team of chefs are dedicated to providing healthy, nutritious (and delicious) meals at lunchtimes.
We use a cashless system for school lunches called School Gateway. To top up your child’s lunch account click here.

For information on school uniform and PE kit, click here.
Support for Students
Each year group is split into two separate Pastoral groups. Pupils are placed in mixed ability groups led by a Pastoral Tutor and Support Tutor. The Pastoral programme helps pupils to prepare for the day ahead. They are encouraged to build relationships and have more informal conversations within their pastoral group. These twice daily touch-points also allow pupils to regulate and discuss any issues or concerns with a trusted adult. Pastoral meetings for teaching and support staff are held weekly to discuss any issues concerning pupils and identify how these can be addressed.
For more information on how we support our students with their individual needs, please see our SEN Provision page.

Curriculum
Curriculum Statement
The curriculum at Alfriston School provides an experience that is broad and balanced and reflects each individual pupil’s learning needs. We enable our pupils to meet their full educational potential, to make progress in their learning, their behaviour and their spiritual, moral, social and cultural development.
There are aspects to our curriculum that are similar to many mainstream schools, but class sizes are smaller and staff to student ratios are higher. In addition, we also provide lessons during which pupils can learn and practice the skills needed in order to fully access and enjoy life in school and beyond.
The timetabled curriculum at Key Stage 3 includes subjects for all pupils that are recognisable from mainstream settings: English, Maths, Science, Religion and Ethics, PE and PSHE. These are presented alongside subjects which enrich our pupils’ lives and facilitate enjoyment and successful participation in community life beyond school: Art, Music, Dance, Drama, Design Craft, Home Economics, Forest School, Social Skills and Environmental Studies.
The curriculum at Key Stage 4 and 5 provides many individual learning pathways for our students. In Key Stage 4 all students continue to study English, Maths, Science, Religion and Ethics, PE and PSHE. Enrichment and preparation for life beyond school is facilitated through dance, work related learning, participation in the Duke of Edinburgh’s award scheme and through the use of half termly optional units of study which target individual need. The optional units provide cultural enrichment, engagement with community organisations, and the development of both prevocational and vocational skills and competences. The role of enrichment and preparation for transition beyond school is further developed in Key Stage 5 with students accessing work experience, community engagement and college link courses alongside aspects of the Key Stage 4 programme.

Wellbeing and Therapies
Aims and Intent
Wellbeing and therapeutic provision at Alfriston is overseen by Emma Collier-Radford, Deputy Head for Inclusion and Belonging.
Our approach is rooted in understanding the relationship between our students’ special educational needs and/or disabilities (SEND), their wellbeing, and their ability to thrive in all aspects of school life and beyond.
At Alfriston, we believe that all staff are responsible for meeting the diverse educational and wellbeing needs of our students. We have updated our policies, practices, and staff training to reflect this belief, forming the foundation of our universal provision for wellbeing and therapies.
Universal Provision
All students at Alfriston have access to:
A PSHE curriculum that addresses mental wellbeing
Targeted Provision
Some students may require additional targeted support from the Wellbeing and Therapies Team.
This may include small group interventions, mentoring, or short-term programmes focused on specific needs such as emotional regulation, activities of daily living, or social skills. These supports are typically time-limited and regularly reviewed to assess their impact.
Targeted support addresses the provision outlined in Section F of a student’s EHCP that is not met through our universal offer.
Specialist Provision
Specialist provision is designed for students with more complex or persistent needs that cannot be met through universal or targeted support alone. This often involves a high level of direct input from SALT, OT, or external professionals such as educational psychologists, health services, CAMHS, or social care.
Targeted and Specialist Provision
Alfriston is fortunate to employ a wide range of professionals who deliver targeted and specialist input across three key strands
Talking Therapies and Interventions
Expressive Therapies
We also work closely with external agencies to address the holistic needs of our students. These include (but are not limited to):
Counselling
Mentoring
Art Therapy
Music Therapy
Drawing and Talking
Speech and Language Therapy (SALT)
Occupational Therapy (OT)
Medical care plans
Mental Health Support Team
Healthcare specialists
Educational Psychology
Virtual School
Family Support Service
Social Care
Post-Adoption Team
Referrals and Requests for Targeted/Specialist Support
If you believe your child would benefit from targeted or specialist support from the Wellbeing and Therapies Team, or from a referral to an external agency, please contact your child’s pastoral tutor.
The pastoral tutor will pass the request to the Wellbeing and Therapies Team, who will review it using a multidisciplinary approach.
Multidisciplinary Approach
The inclusion of a wide range of professionals within our team enables us to take a multidisciplinary approach to supporting students. This is essential in creating a holistic and responsive support system, particularly for students whose needs are often co-occurring and do not exist in isolation.
By bringing together professionals from education, health, and mental health services, Alfriston ensures that the diverse and often complex needs of pupils are understood and addressed in a coordinated way. This collaborative model promotes early identification of issues, shared responsibility, and consistent communication between agencies—leading to more effective interventions and improved outcomes.
